model: Orbital Economy v7.7.12 Food candidate r1
note: Task 032 fragment. Covers every new exogenous food parameter required by TASK_RU §2: Food Enabled, the 20 declaration parameters, five asymmetric A/B pairs (annotation on A with applies_to_mirror), and the two non-zero B→A startup trade stocks. Food transport labor is intentionally not modeled at Planet v2 step 2.

Food Enabled.role: Food-layer switch; default 0, enabled only by new Modes 49–51.
Food Enabled.effect: At 0 every food replacement selects the previous formula; at 1 food/farms/trade and their feedbacks are active.

Food Need per Capita.role: Daily food need per person, value 1 food unit/person/day.
Food Need per Capita.effect: Scales regional Food Demand directly with Population.

Food Energy per Unit.role: Farm energy intensity, value 0.5 energy units per unit of planned food production.
Food Energy per Unit.effect: Scales Farming Requested Energy and therefore priority-energy demand from farms.

Food Labor per Unit.role: Farm labor intensity, value 0.15 labor units per unit of food production.
Food Labor per Unit.effect: Scales Farming Labor Requirement; labor remains accounting-only at Planet v2 step 2.

Food Freight Weight per Unit.role: Shared-transport weight of food, value 0.5 transport-load units per food unit.
Food Freight Weight per Unit.effect: Converts food dispatch into Food Transport Load and therefore reduces capacity left for ordinary goods.

Food Transport Max Share.role: Maximum share of shared transport reserved for food, value 0.8.
Food Transport Max Share.effect: Caps food transport capacity at 80% of Transport Active Throughput Capacity before ordinary goods use the remainder.

Farm Capital Goods per Capacity.role: Capital-goods requirement for farm expansion, value 0.3 goods per unit of farm capacity.
Farm Capital Goods per Capacity.effect: Converts Farm Expansion into capital-goods consumption and added Capital Goods Demand.

Farm Depreciation Rate.role: Farm depreciation rate, 0.0000555555555556 per model day (2% per 360-day model year).
Farm Depreciation Rate.effect: Removes Farm Capacity through Farm Depreciation while food is enabled.

Farm Capacity Adjustment Time.role: Farm capacity adjustment time, 360 model days.
Farm Capacity Adjustment Time.effect: Sets the rate at which desired additional farm capacity is converted into Farm Desired Expansion.

Farm Desired Capacity Margin.effect: Targets farm capacity at 115% of the production signal, subject to the land cap.

Food Target Coverage Days.effect: Sets initial Food Inventory and the inventory target used by production/import planning and Food Price.

Food Inventory Adjustment Time.effect: Controls how quickly shortages/excess relative to target stock alter desired production and import need.

Food Buffer Days.role: Coverage needed for full immediate fulfillment, 5 model days.
Food Buffer Days.effect: Maps Food Coverage Days to Food Fulfillment; five buffer days or more gives fulfillment 1.

Food Demand Signal Time.effect: Controls adjustment of Food Demand Signal toward current population-driven Food Demand.

Food Production Signal Time.effect: Controls Food Production Signal and pairwise Food Export Signal adjustment.

Food Export Release Time.role: Release time for exportable inventory, 5 model days.
Food Export Release Time.effect: Controls how fast inventory above half the target can be offered to importing regions.

Food Price Reference.role: Reference food price, value 10 model price units.
Food Price Reference.effect: Anchors Food Price when coverage is at the target level and normalizes food's contribution to Price Index.

Food Price Elasticity.effect: Controls how strongly Food Price rises as coverage falls below the target.

Famine Death Sensitivity.role: Mortality sensitivity to food fulfillment, exponent 2.
Famine Death Sensitivity.effect: Multiplies the previous death flow by fulfillment^-2 (with the node floor), increasing mortality under food shortage.

Living Food Weight.role: Food exponent in Living Standard, value 0.5.
Living Food Weight.effect: Weights food fulfillment as the square-root factor in the food-enabled living-standard product.

Living Energy Weight With Food.role: Energy exponent in food-enabled Living Standard, value 0.5.
Living Energy Weight With Food.effect: Weights Energy Fulfillment Ratio as the second square-root factor in Living Standard when food is enabled.

A Farm Land Capacity.role: Regional farm-land soft cap. Initial values A=22, B=60; fertile B is an explicit owner decision.
A Farm Land Capacity.effect: Sets the maximum effective/desired farm scale by region and is the primary initial comparative advantage of B.

A Farm Capacity.role: Initial physical farm capacity. Generated start values A=22, B=17.142206601972095 from initial population, land and the start-state export allocation.
A Farm Capacity.effect: Sets the starting productive capital of farms before expansion/depreciation dynamics.
A Farm Capacity.evidence: lab/src/nodes/food.js start-state algorithm; V7_7_12_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC §5 notes B start ≈17.14.

A Food Inventory.role: Initial food stock. A=840, B=255 = initial population (28 / 8.5) × 30 target coverage days.
A Food Inventory.effect: Sets starting coverage and prevents an artificial startup famine while farms/trade begin from the balanced start state.
A Food Inventory.evidence: lab/src/nodes/food.js: Food Inventory initial = population_initial × Food Target Coverage Days.

A Food Demand Signal.role: Initial smoothed food-demand signal. A=28, B=8.5, equal to each region's initial population.
A Food Demand Signal.effect: Seeds demand planning at the pre-food demographic state, avoiding a startup smoothing transient.
A Food Demand Signal.evidence: lab/src/nodes/food.js start-state algorithm: Food Demand Signal initial = population_initial.

A Food Production Signal.role: Initial smoothed production plan. A=20.174088950502767, B=16.325911049497233 after land-limited A and B's assigned startup exports.
A Food Production Signal.effect: Seeds farm energy requests and desired farm capacity at the physically balanced startup production plan.
A Food Production Signal.evidence: lab/src/nodes/food.js start-state algorithm (soft land efficiency plus startup export allocation); V7_7_12_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC §5.

B to A Food Export Signal.role: Initial B→A export-order signal, 7.825911049497232 food units/day; it equals A's land-limited startup shortfall assigned to fertile B.
B to A Food Export Signal.effect: Starts B production planning with A's existing deficit already visible instead of waiting 90 days for the export-order signal to build.
B to A Food Export Signal.evidence: lab/src/nodes/food.js start-state algorithm: A shortfall is allocated to regions with spare land; B is the exporter.

Food Cargo B to A.role: Initial food already in transit B→A, 78.25911049497232 food units = 7.825911049497232/day × 10-day Travel Time.
Food Cargo B to A.effect: Represents the startup export flow already inside the transport delay, preventing a synthetic ten-day delivery gap at model start.
Food Cargo B to A.evidence: lab/src/nodes/food.js start-state algorithm and V7_7_12_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC §1 (10-day cargo transit).
